items.followUp: Define a point-to-point connection and give one daily-life example.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition identifies the link as shared between multiple devices.
rubric.description: Defines a multipoint connection as a communication link shared by two or more devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a shared link and identifying multiple devices.

rubric.why: Checks that a relevant daily-life example is provided.
rubric.description: Gives an example of several devices sharing a wireless router.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable everyday example.

modelAnswer: A multipoint connection is a communication link shared by two or more devices.
For example, several phones and computers can share one wireless router to access the Internet.

rubric.why: Checks that the web server is identified by its role in storing or hosting websites.
rubric.description: Defines a web server as a computer or program that stores or hosts websites.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a computer or program that stores or hosts websites.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer explains how a web server provides website content.
rubric.description: States that it responds to a client request by sending web pages.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its response to a request.

modelAnswer: A web server is a computer or program that stores and hosts websites.
It responds to a client request by sending the requested web pages.

items.followUp: Write an HTML tag that creates a hyperlink to another webpage.

rubric.why: Checks that the purpose of a hyperlink is explained.
rubric.description: States that a hyperlink connects to another webpage, document, or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining what a hyperlink connects to.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer describes a correct way to create or use a hyperlink.
rubric.description: Gives an anchor tag with an href attribute or explains that the user clicks linked text.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct HTML method or clear description of its use.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink connects a webpage to another webpage, document, or location.
In HTML, it is made with an anchor tag, for example: Open page; the user clicks the linked text to open it.

items.followUp: Describe how you identify the inputs and outputs when designing an algorithm.

rubric.why: Checks that the problem and its requirements are considered before writing the algorithm.
rubric.description: States that the problem and its requirements must be understood or analysed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying problem analysis as a step.

rubric.why: Checks that the required input data is identified.
rubric.description: States that the data needed to solve the problem must be determined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the inputs.

rubric.why: Checks that the required result is identified.
rubric.description: States that the required output or result must be determined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the output.

rubric.why: Checks that the solution is expressed in steps and tested.
rubric.description: States that the solution is arranged as logical steps and the algorithm is tested.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the stepwise solution and its testing.

modelAnswer: First, understand and analyse the problem and its requirements.
Identify the input data needed to solve the problem.
Determine the output or result that is required.
Arrange the solution as logical steps, then test the algorithm to check that it works correctly.

items.followUp: Define invalid test data and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks that validity is defined in relation to the program's requirements.
rubric.description: States that valid test data satisfies the requirements specified for a program.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking valid data to the program's requirements.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer identifies an acceptable condition for valid input.
rubric.description: States that valid data is acceptable for processing, such as having the correct type or falling within the permitted range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant condition for acceptable input.

modelAnswer: Valid test data is input data that satisfies the requirements specified for a program.
It is acceptable for the program to process, for example because it has the correct type or falls within the permitted range.
